subject: philosophy

source.document: A-level Philosophy (7172) Specification — for teaching from September 2017 onwards, A-level exams June 2019 onwards, version 1.1 August 2026
source.track: A Level · ages 16–19 · linear two-year course · Paper 1 Epistemology and moral philosophy, Paper 2 The metaphysics of God and the metaphysics of mind

note: Units follow the specification's subject content in order: the required language of argumentation, then 3.1 Epistemology, 3.2 Moral philosophy, 3.3 Metaphysics of God and 3.4 Metaphysics of mind, numbered by their own subsections. A few live lessons sit in the units they genuinely serve even where they reach past the named content (free will under God's foreknowledge, AI ethics under applied ethics); a closing atlas-only unit tracks the rest so nothing is orphaned.

program.title: The language of argumentation
topics: Identify argument within text
The structure of argument: premises, reasons, conclusions and inferences
Forms of argument: deduction and induction (including abduction)
Validity/invalidity and soundness/unsoundness
Arguments from analogy and hypothetical reasoning (including Ockham's Razor)
Flaws in argument: circularity, contradictions, question-begging and other fallacies
Philosophical terminology: analytic/synthetic, a priori/a posteriori, necessary/contingent

program.title: What is knowledge?
topics: 3.1.1 Acquaintance knowledge, ability knowledge and propositional knowledge
The nature of definition (Linda Zagzebski)
The tripartite view: justified true belief
Issues with the tripartite view: Gettier's counterexamples and lucky true beliefs
Post-Gettier responses: infallibilism, no false lemmas, reliabilism, epistemic virtue

program.title: Perception as a source of knowledge
topics: 3.1.2 Direct realism and the arguments from illusion, perceptual variation, hallucination and time-lag
Indirect realism: sense-data and Locke's primary/secondary quality distinction
Responses to scepticism about mind-independent objects: Locke, Trotter Cockburn, Russell's 'best hypothesis'
Berkeley's Idealism: the attack on primary/secondary qualities and the 'Master' argument
Issues for idealism: solipsism and the role of God

program.title: Reason as a source of knowledge
topics: 3.1.3 Innatism: Plato's 'slave boy' argument and Leibniz's argument from necessary truths
Empiricist responses: Locke's 'tabula rasa', impressions and ideas
The intuition and deduction thesis: Descartes' clear and distinct ideas
The cogito, the arguments for the existence of God and the proof of the external world
Hume's Fork and empiricist responses to Descartes

program.title: The limits of knowledge
topics: 3.1.4 Philosophical scepticism and normal incredulity
Local and global scepticism
Descartes' sceptical arguments: the three 'waves of doubt'
Responses to scepticism: Descartes, Locke, Berkeley, Russell and reliabilism

program.title: Normative ethical theories
topics: 3.2.1 Utilitarianism: Bentham's quantitative hedonism and the utility calculus
Mill's qualitative hedonism, the 'proof' of the greatest happiness principle and preference utilitarianism
Act and rule utilitarianism and issues: the experience machine, tyranny of the majority, calculation, partiality
Kantian deontological ethics: the good will, acting out of duty, hypothetical and categorical imperatives
The two formulations of the categorical imperative and issues: clashing duties, Foot's hypothetical imperatives
Aristotelian virtue ethics: eudaimonia as the final end and the function argument
Virtues and vices, the doctrine of the mean, moral responsibility and practical wisdom

program.title: Applied ethics
topics: 3.2.2 Applying normative ethical theories and meta-ethics to stealing
Simulated killing (within computer games, plays, films etc)
Eating animals
Telling lies

program.title: Meta-ethics
topics: 3.2.3 The origins of moral principles: reason, emotion/attitudes, or society
Cognitivism and non-cognitivism about ethical language
Moral realism: moral naturalism, moral non-naturalism, Moore's open question argument
Issues: Hume's Fork, the is-ought gap, Mackie's arguments from relativity and queerness
Moral anti-realism: Mackie's error theory, Ayer's emotivism, Hare's prescriptivism

program.title: The concept and nature of 'God'
topics: 3.3.1 God as omniscient, omnipotent and supremely good (omnibenevolent)
God timeless (eternal) or God within time (everlasting)
Arguments for the incoherence of the concept of God: the paradox of the stone
The Euthyphro dilemma
The compatibility, or otherwise, of an omniscient God and free human beings

program.title: Arguments relating to the existence of God
topics: 3.3.2 Ontological arguments: St Anselm, Descartes, Norman Malcolm
Objections to the ontological argument: Gaunilo's 'perfect island', Kant on existence not being a predicate
Teleological/design arguments: Hume's argument from analogy, Paley's spatial order, Swinburne's temporal order
Cosmological arguments: the Kalām argument, Aquinas' 1st, 2nd and 3rd ways, Leibniz's principle of sufficient reason
The Problem of Evil: moral and natural evil, logical and evidential forms
Responses: the Free Will Defence (Plantinga) and soul-making (Hick)

program.title: Religious language
topics: 3.3.3 Cognitivism and non-cognitivism about religious language
The verification principle and falsification (Ayer)
Hick's response: eschatological verification
The University Debate: Flew on falsification, Mitchell's Partisan, Hare's bliks

program.title: What do we mean by 'mind'?
topics: 3.4.1 Phenomenal properties of mental states (qualia)
Intentional properties of mental states (intentionality)

program.title: Dualist theories
topics: 3.4.2 Substance dualism: Descartes' indivisibility and conceivability arguments
Property dualism: Chalmers' 'philosophical zombies' and Jackson's knowledge/Mary argument
The problem of other minds and Ryle's category mistake
The interaction problem (Elisabeth, Princess of Bohemia) and epiphenomenalist dualism

program.title: Physicalist theories
topics: 3.4.3 Physicalism: everything is physical or supervenes upon the physical
Philosophical behaviourism: Hempel's 'hard' behaviourism and Ryle's 'soft' behaviourism
Mind-brain type identity theory and the multiple realisability of mental states
Eliminative materialism (Patricia and Paul Churchland)

program.title: Functionalism
topics: 3.4.4 Mental states characterised by functional roles, multiply realised
Inverted qualia and Ned Block's 'China' thought experiment
The knowledge/Mary argument applied to functional facts

program.title: Wider philosophy: atlas extension
topics: Metaphysics: objects, properties, time and possibility
Political philosophy: the social contract
Philosophy of science: induction, demarcation and Kuhn
Eastern philosophy: Vedanta to Zen
Aesthetics: beauty, taste and the art-argument
